# vaultwarden_item_secure_note (Resource)

This resource creates a secure note item in the personal vault of the provider user or in an organization. The note's text is the `notes` attribute.

Items are encrypted client-side, like Bitwarden clients do: new items get their own item key (cipher key), which is encrypted with the key of the provider user or of the organization. Updates keep the parts of the item that the provider does not manage, such as the password history, passkeys and attachments. Deleting the item deletes it permanently, without moving it to the trash. An item moved to the trash outside Terraform is created again.

The secrets of the item, such as `notes`, are saved in the Terraform state. Requires `email` and `master_password` to be set in the provider configuration.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "vaultwarden_item_secure_note" "example" {
  name  = "Recovery instructions"
  notes = <<-EOT
    1. Restore the latest backup.
    2. Rotate the credentials.
  EOT
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) The name of the item

### Optional

- `collection_ids` (Set of String) IDs of the organization collections the item is assigned to. Requires `organization_id`. Defaults to none, which only organization owners and admins can use; other members must assign the item to a collection they can edit
- `favorite` (Boolean) Whether the item is a favorite of the provider user. Defaults to `false`
- `fields` (Attributes List) The custom fields of the item. Defaults to none (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--fields))
- `folder_id` (String) ID of the provider user's folder that the item is in. Folders are personal: the item is shown in the folder only for the provider user, also for organization items
- `notes` (String, Sensitive) The notes of the item
- `organization_id` (String) ID of the organization that owns the item. Leave unset for an item in the personal vault of the provider user. Changing it replaces the item, because Bitwarden cannot move items out of an organization
- `reprompt` (Boolean) Whether Bitwarden clients ask for the master password before showing the item. Defaults to `false`

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) ID of the item

<a id="nestedatt--fields"></a>
### Nested Schema for `fields`

Optional:

- `linked_id` (Number) For a `linked` field, the ID of the item attribute it links to, such as `100` for the username or `101` for the password of a login
- `name` (String) The name of the custom field
- `type` (String) The type of the custom field: `text`, `hidden`, `boolean` or `linked`. Defaults to `text`
- `value` (String, Sensitive) The value of the custom field. For a `boolean` field, `true` or `false`. Linked fields have no value

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import vaultwarden_item_secure_note.example <item_id>
```
